changes: Started as three LOW cleanups and grew, through four review-driven scope expansions, into a durable audit guarantee. (1) transition-orchestrator.ts: buildPhaseTransitionProcessEvent gained optional transitionType/reason appended only when defined, and the call site passes them only when eventType==='REOPEN', so a gated PLAN->INIT reopen leaves its operator reason in the append-only phase_transition event while normal transitions keep a byte-identical shape. (2) Same file: the REOPEN checklist-reset comment now states its real guarantee (concurrency-atomic via the mkdir persist claim, ordered phase-write-last) instead of 'land together or not at all'. (3) worktree.ts: the pruneWorktreeRegistry comment documents that `git worktree prune --expire now` cannot remove a live sibling, is repo-wide not story-scoped, and that a locked worktree survives even with its directory gone. (4) process-fact-registry.ts + scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs: the reopen audit semantics are DECLARED and MECHANICALLY ASSERTED, satisfying the dual-layer process-fact contract so the guarantee cannot be silently refactored away. (5) The reopen audit record now lands in the SAME atomic writeStory rename as phase=INIT, with reconcilePendingReopenAudit at the top of every transition, so a crash between the phase write and the event append is recoverable rather than an unaudited reopen. (6) reconcileReopenAuditBeforeOutOfBandPhaseChange rescues the record at the two out-of-band phase mutators (story_discard in worktree.ts, zombie DONE repair in story-query.ts), reading from the doomed worktree copy and appending to the surviving log. (7) types.ts declares the pendingReopenAudit recovery field. plan-init-reopen-roundtrip-smoke.ts now carries 6 fault-injection drills. (8) After a third independent cross-host MAJOR finding, the guarantee was NARROWED rather than overclaimed: story_discard's rescue holds no per-story fence, so a reopen RACING a concurrent discard is still lost. The code, types.ts, both call sites, the process-fact registry rationale and the mechanical verifier now all state the SEQUENTIAL-only guarantee and name the race as a known residual; re-inflating the wording fails verify-process-fact-contract. The concurrency hardening is tracked as B-META-framework-audit:F-003 (committed to main as b5842ec40d).
usage: lattice story_advance '{"storyId":"B-xxxx","phase":"INIT","reason":"why the frozen title must change"}' from PLAN. The reason is then durably readable in .lattice/story/actives/B-xxxx/process-events.jsonl as a phase_transition event with transitionType=reopen. `npm run test:process-fact-contract` mechanically enforces the semantics; a crash mid-transition is reconciled on the next transition, and story_discard / story_reconcile rescue the record before destroying it.
expectedOutcome: A maintainer who reopens a story to INIT can prove WHY afterwards: the reason survives a crash between the phase write and the event append, and survives a story_discard or repairing story_reconcile that destroys the worktree holding it — SEQUENTIALLY. A reopen racing a concurrent terminal operation is NOT recovered; that residual is stated in the code, the registry and the mechanical contract, and is tracked as its own follow-up. The guarantee cannot be silently widened or refactored away, because the contract fails if the wording is re-inflated or the marker/reason dropped.
actualTranscript: npm --prefix packages/main run build -> exit 0. node packages/main/dist/tasks/plan-init-reopen-roundtrip-smoke.js -> 6 drills pass incl. '✓ same-reason reopens are audited separately' (exit 0). node packages/main/dist/tasks/flow-stability-smoke.js -> '✓ flow stability smoke passed'. npm run test:process-fact-contract -> 'Process fact contract verified'. done_required_validate -> PASS (packages/main build exit 0 + root full `npm test` exit 0). grep -c 'land together or not at all' transition-orchestrator.ts -> 0. grep -c 'live sibling' worktree.ts -> 2. RED PROOFS, each in an isolated scratch copy and each COMPILING CLEAN under tsc (so this class is provably not catchable by the build): F-003 7 mutations, F-004 12/13 mutations, F-005 11/11 mutations, round-5 8 mutations — every one flipped the contract or smoke to exit 1 and reverting restored exit 0.
outcomeDiff: The delivered scope is MUCH larger than requested, entirely because independent review found real defects. The original ask was three LOW cleanups (deliverables 1-3). Deliverables 4-7 were added after: an independent cross-host reviewer (codex-host-b) returned FAIL twice, first for missing process-fact registration (F-003) and then for the audit event being appended after the phase write and after the persist claim was released, leaving an UNRECOVERABLE unaudited reopen (F-004); then a behavior reviewer proved the resulting invariant was still falsifiable via story_discard (F-005). Notably the main agent had explicitly and WRONGLY argued the F-004 class of concern was merely a pre-existing universal property and excluded it from scope — the requester had asked for exactly this in their original section 5, and they were right. Two deviations from the original request remain deliberate: actor/eventId provenance excluded per scope-boundary.json after the requester answered 'no preference'; and full crash-transactionality was not achieved (the window is made RECOVERABLE, not eliminated). FINAL POSITION ON THE THIRD FINDING: the reviewer's suggested lock-based fix was investigated and DECLINED, because acquireStoryTransitionLock is documented as a best-effort advisory contention-reducer that an env var turns into a no-op (so no guarantee can rest on it), it exposes no failFastIfHeld and so polls a 180s deadline before throwing, and classifyTransitionLockHolder never stale-reclaims a leaked lock whose pid was recycled by a live process — all disqualifying on story_discard, the recovery command operators reach for when things are already stuck. A non-blocking try-acquire was also rejected, because the orchestrator takes the lock before its own readStory, so a genuinely racing reopen defeats it anyway while leaving a mutex that reads as serialization the function does not have. Narrowing the claim was chosen over shipping a guarantee that was not real.
limitations: The audit event records reason/transitionType/fromPhase/toPhase/timestamp but NOT actor or eventId. The guarantee is SEQUENTIAL: a reopen whose record is already on disk when a terminal operation starts is recovered; a reopen RACING a concurrent story_discard or repairing story_reconcile is NOT — that race is real, unfixed, documented in all layers, and tracked as B-META-framework-audit:F-003. A second lock-independent case: story_discard --force when the worktree is already gone has nothing to rescue, since the record only ever lived there. The two-write window is made RECOVERABLE, not eliminated. Recovery fires on orchestrated transitions plus the two out-of-band phase mutators, never on read-only commands. The already-audited check is read-then-append, not atomic CAS; its failure mode is a duplicate event sharing one auditId (dedupable), never a lost one. The doomed copy's record is deliberately not cleared, to avoid dirtying a worktree a non-force discard would then refuse. story_discard --purge removes the log including the rescued event — an explicit erase, now warned about. No lattice doctor orphaned-record check was added (doctor was outside scope); that remains an advisory gap. The registry entry is audit-only history, NOT gate evidence.
pitfalls: Six lessons. (1) Driving lattice from a NESTED git worktree makes INIT_CHECK's reconcile resolve a double-nested path and die with a misleading 'spawnSync git ENOENT'; it split story metadata across two branches and needed cherry-picking to recover. (2) The validate suite is 51 commands and exceeds story_advance's 900s watchdog; every TEST/DONE advance needs LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS raised. (3) Pre-writing a 'reference implementation' before dispatching implementers is a trap — independent implementers found real defects in ALL THREE original commits. (4) verification_evidence_refresh_stale will rebind ANY stale evidence including one whose command was the DESTRUCTIVE 'git worktree prune --expire now -v' and one using a moving 'git diff HEAD~1'; re-run evidence commands yourself before refreshing. (5) CLOSEOUT ORDERING: every metadata auto-commit moves materialHash and stales evidence, delivery-check and the assurance floor — update summary.json BEFORE the delivery reviewer signs, and bind the floor LAST. (6) THE BIG ONE: the local Claude reviewer panel passed a MAJOR defect across TWO rounds and a second MAJOR defect across FOUR; both were caught only by the independent cross-host reviewer, and a third by a reviewer role not in the default roster. Do not treat local-panel consensus as sufficient for a load-bearing guarantee. Also: a naive fix for F-005 would have been a silent no-op, because cli/runtime-root.ts redirects story_discard's root away from the worktree holding the record — always verify the fix actually executes on the path it claims to protect. (7) A justification can be confidently wrong: one recorded blocker cited the transition-cas persist claim (staleMs 15000) when the actual candidate primitive was acquireStoryTransitionLock (staleMs 120000) — caught by a reviewer, retracted in place rather than silently swapped. (8) An uncommitted tracking record is not tracking: 'tracked as B-META...' was written while the file was still only in main's working tree; a reviewer checked committed state and correctly called it false. Commit the tracker before citing it.
